newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish want shamrock back as symbol of Emerald Isle.
newsitem.headline: Irish want shamrock back as symbol of Emerald Isle.

text.p: Ireland's new government wants the shamrock reinstated as the logo for tourism instead of what baffled citizens think is a football, a Viking ship or even two hairy monsters.

"It is something I feel very strongly about. I am personally committed to the shamrock as our traditional symbol and I don't think we should dispense with it," Tourism Minister Jim McDaid told the Irish Independent.
Bord Failte, the state tourism body, spent 100,000 punts ($150,000) to replace the traditional three-leaf clover last November with a new national symbol for promoting tourism.
But the new logo, which can be seen as two people with arms outstretched, can also be interpreted as anything from a ship to monsters and caused controversy immediately.
"In my opinion there was absolutely no need to get rid of the shamrock. I don't think the 100,000 was well spent," the minister said.
